topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and defines the scope of topics covering environmental exposures and carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer: Intrinsic Mutational Processes and Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental etiology of cancer by evaluating how endogenous biological processes, inherited genetics, and external environmental exposures contribute to malignancy.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents induce DNA damage, metabolic activation, or tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the experimental, epidemiological, and genomic approaches used to identify and determine the carcinogenicity and mutagenicity of exposures.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides final concluding remarks on cancer causation and frames exposure risks in the context of everyday benefit-risk assessment.
